name: Ahumai
title: Descendant of Judah through Shobal, Reajah and Jahath
summary: In the genealogies in 1 Chronicles, Ahumai appears as part of the detailed family register of the tribe of Judah. He was the son of Jahath and brother of Lahad, and together they are regarded as ancestors of the clans of the Zorathites—a group connected with the city of Zorah in the Shephelah lowlands. Ahumai’s paternal line extends through Reaiah back to Shobal, who is linked to the founding of Kiriath-Jearim, a city of great religious and strategic importance for Judah. Although Ahumai is not connected with specific events, his place in the genealogy testifies to the thorough documentation of the branches of the tribe of Judah. These genealogical records served to establish family continuity and support the tribe’s territorial connection to central cities and areas in the promised land.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
keyEvents.description: Ahumai is listed as a son of Jahath in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. He and his brother Lahad are considered ancestors of the clans of the Zorathites.

keyEvents.title: Part of Shobal's lineage
keyEvents.description: Ahumai belonged to the lineage of Shobal through his father Jahath and grandfather Reajah. Shobal is mentioned among the sons of Hur and is regarded as the founder of Kiriath-Jearim. This lineage was connected to the city of Zorah and was prominent within the tribe of Judah.

versions.summary: Ahumai is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of Judah. He was the son of Jahath and belonged to the clan of the Zorathites. He is primarily known through his place in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
versions.title: Descendant of Judah
versions.reason: [major] Ahumai is mentioned in a genealogy in 1 Chronicles 4, but his placement in the family tree (as a descendant of Judah through Shobal and Jahath) likely places him in a much earlier period than the united monarchy. The genealogies in 1 Chronicles extend back to the patriarchal and judges periods. Given the connection to Zorah and the early clans of Judah, 'judges' or 'patriarchs' is more appropriate. 'Judges' is chosen here as a reasonable estimate.; [minor] The roles array is empty. Although Ahumai is a genealogical figure, he should have at least one role describing his function, such as 'Ancestor in Judah' or similar.; [minor] There are four keyEvents for a figure mentioned only in one verse (1 Chron 4:2). These overlap significantly. It would be more precise to reduce them to fewer, more distinct events.; [minor] The title 'Ancestor of the Zorathites' is misleading. The text states that the clans of the Zorathites came from Jahath (through Reajah/Shobal), not specifically that Ahumai was their ancestor. Ahumai was part of these clans, not necessarily their founder.; [minor] The summary is acceptable but could be improved by noting that Ahumai belonged to the lineage of Shobal, son of Hur, to provide more context.

versions.summary: Ahumai is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of Judah. He was the son of Jahath and belonged to the Zorathite clans, which were associated with the city of Zorah in Judah. Through his paternal line, he descends from Shobal, son of Hur, who was a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah. Ahumai is primarily known through his place in the genealogy, and his name is preserved as part of the detailed documentation of the tribal lines of Judah in the books of Chronicles.
versions.title: Descendant of Judah through Shobal and Jahath
versions.reason: [minor] Ahumai is mentioned only in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles, and there is no specific time reference placing him in the period of the judges. The genealogy suggests he belonged to the patriarchal era or an early period. Nevertheless, 'judges' is a reasonable estimate given his lineage's position between Hur and the Zorathites (linked to the Samson narratives), so this can be retained with reservation.; [minor] According to 1 Chron 4:1-2, the lineage is: Judah → Perez → Hezron → ... → Shobal → Reaiah → Jahath → Ahumai. Reaiah is mentioned as Shobal's son and Jahath's father in verse 2. This is correctly reflected in the summary, but 'father' is assigned to 'Jahath' – this is correct. Everything matches.; [minor] The title mentions 'Shobal and Jahath', but Reaiah is a link between Shobal and Jahath (Shobal → Reaiah → Jahath). The title could have been more precise by including Reaiah, but it is acceptable as a simplified description.; [minor] The summary states, "Through his paternal line he descends from Shobal, son of Hur." In 1 Chron 4:1-2, it is Reaiah who is the son of Shobal, and Jahath is the son of Reaiah. Reaiah should be mentioned for completeness. Furthermore, it is 1 Chron 2:50 that states Shobal was the son of Hur – this intermediate link should be clarified.

versions.summary: Ahumai is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of Judah. He was the son of Jahath and brother of Lahad, and belonged to the clans of the Zorathites, who were connected with the city of Zorah in Judah. Through his father's line, Ahumai can be traced back through Reaiah to Shobal, who in turn was the son of Hur – a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah. Shobal is referred to as the founder of Kiriath-Jearim, which shows the clan's connection with central cities in Judah. Ahumai is primarily known through his place in the genealogy, and his name is preserved as part of the detailed documentation of the tribal lines of Judah that served to strengthen the tribe's identity and territorial claims.
versions.title: Descendant of Judah through Shobal, Reajah and Jahath
versions.reason: [minor] Ahumai is primarily known from the genealogies in 1 Chronicles, which were compiled after the exile. However, the person himself is placed in Judah's early lineage. 'Judges' is a reasonable assumption given the familial connection to Zorah and the period of Samson, but strictly speaking it remains uncertain. It is retained as is, since this is the most likely placement.; [minor] The summary is good and informative, but versions 1 and 2 had similar opening phrases. The current version is more detailed, though it could have an even more distinct opening. Nevertheless, the content is theologically sound and significantly improved.; [minor] Shobal is mentioned as Ahumai's ancestor through Reaiah and Jahath, but Shobal's father Hur could also have been noted in the keyEvents description. However, this is not a direct family connection that should be included in the family object, so this remains only an observation.; [minor] The description states "Shobal was the son of Hur," but according to 1 Chron 2:50, Shobal was the son of Caleb (through Hur/Ephrathah). The relationship between Shobal and Hur is somewhat ambiguous – in 1 Chron 2:50, Shobal is listed among the sons of Hur, son of Ephrathah, while in 4:1-2, Shobal is listed as a son of Judah. The description should be nuanced slightly.

footnotes.text: The name Ahumai (אֲחוּמַי) has an uncertain etymology. Some scholars have suggested it may mean 'brother of water' or 'my brother is water,' from the Hebrew elements אח (akh, 'brother') and מַיִם (mayim, 'water'), but this is uncertain. Others have linked it to a root meaning 'heated' or 'hot.'

The Zorathites (צָרְעָתִי) were associated with the city of Zorah (Tsora), which was located in the Shephelah lowlands between the hill country of Judah and the coastal plain. The city is known from the Samson narratives (Judg 13:2, 25) and was an important boundary point between Judah and Dan.

The genealogies in 1 Chronicles chapters 1–9 were likely compiled after the Babylonian exile to document family lines and land rights for those who returned. They served as a basis for legitimizing tribal affiliation and territorial claims in the rebuilt community.

Shobal, mentioned as Ahumai's ancestor, is described in 1 Chron 2:52 as 'father of Kiriath-jearim.' This shows how the genealogies in Chronicles connect clans to specific cities and geographic areas in Judah.

Reaiah, who according to 1 Chron 4:2 was Shobal's son and Jahath's father, serves as an important link in the lineage between Shobal and Ahumai. The name Reaiah (רְאָיָה) may mean 'the Lord has seen,' connecting it to a theophoric tradition in Hebrew personal names.

Kiriath-jearim, to which Shobal is linked, was an important city where the ark of the covenant was kept for a long period after it was returned by the Philistines (1 Sam 7:1–2). The city lay on the border between Judah and Benjamin and had both religious and strategic significance.
